claims.text: Replacing EAM reference potentials with an MLP trained directly on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
The proposed scope includes alloys with four or more principal elements at temperatures near or above 0.9 Tm.
The MLP should be trained using ab initio molecular-dynamics data from the liquid phase.
High-temperature ab initio liquid configurations in compositionally complex alloys are diverse.
Conventional EAM potentials are unable to capture the anharmonicity and disorder needed to represent these liquids.
Training on ab initio liquid data enables the MLP to capture a broader range of atomic configurations than the EAM reference.
The trained MLP will sample configurations that more closely mirror the target ab initio potential's configurations.
Improved configurational overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will reduce error accumulation in calculated free-energy differences.
The MLP reference should reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD using EAM references.
The MLP reference should produce free-energy estimates that agree better with independent ab initio benchmarks.
TOR-TILD's EAM references have known limitations in describing the configuration space of high-temperature liquids in multicomponent alloys.
The benefit of an MLP reference may diminish in elemental metals or dilute binary alloys.
The benefit may diminish far below melting because liquid anharmonic effects are less pronounced there.
Insufficient ab initio training data could limit MLP performance.
Improvement will vary with alloy composition and temperature.
A reduction in path mismatch below approximately 30%, together with no marked overlap improvement and free-energy results statistically equivalent to EAM results, would falsify the hypothesis.
